change.title: pr-2
change.description: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: Unsubscribe flips the level on every GET, so a reload moves it again
findings.body: `unsubscribe` toggles instead of setting a value: above regular it sets regular, otherwise muted (lines 107-111). The route is a GET (config/routes.rb:440-441), and the browser re-requests the page on reload, and on Back when it does not restore from cache. Each fresh request changes the level again, e.g. watching -> regular -> muted over two reloads, with no user action and no change in the page text. The Ember route only reads the preloaded payload on first entry (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/post-stream.js.es6:821-823), so the server request is the one that toggles. Make the write idempotent: set the level the email promises (muted), rather than toggling.
findings.originReason: The unsubscribe action and its toggle logic are new in this diff.

verification.reason: The action changes the level based on its current value: anything above regular becomes regular, otherwise muted. The route is a GET, so each full reload is a new write. Watching goes to regular on the first load and muted on the next. The Ember route loads /t/:id.json, not the unsubscribe action, so only the server GET writes.

findings.title: Notification level is changed on GET, so any page can trigger it for a logged-in user
findings.body: `protect_from_forgery` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:21) checks only non-GET requests, and `unsubscribe` writes on GET (config/routes.rb:440-441). A third-party page can load `/t///unsubscribe` in a logged-in user's browser (e.g. an tag) and change that user's notification level for the topic. Fix: keep the email link as a landing page that shows the state, and perform the write from that page with a non-GET request.
findings.originReason: The GET action that writes state is added by this diff.

verification.reason: `protect_from_forgery` only checks non-GET requests, and `unsubscribe` is a GET that writes the user's TopicUser level. Any cross-site GET made with the user's cookies changes their notification level.

findings.title: tu.save! skips the reason stamp, so reading the topic can re-subscribe the user
findings.body: `TopicUser.change` stamps notifications_reason_id (user_changed) and notifications_changed_at whenever a level is set (app/models/topic_user.rb:87-89). `unsubscribe` writes with `save!` and sets neither, so the reason stays nil. The mailer creates the recipient's row without a reason (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:312 calls TopicUser.change with no notification_level, topic_user.rb:77-106). In `update_last_read`, a row with a null reason is switched to tracking once the time read passes the threshold (app/models/topic_user.rb:161-163). A user who unsubscribes and later reads the topic is therefore silently re-subscribed. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic.id, notification_level: ...)`, as `set_notifications` does (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:330-334).
findings.originReason: The save! write path is new in this diff.

verification.reason: `tu.save!` sets only notification_level, and TopicUser has no callback that sets the reason. A row created by the mailer's TopicUser.change (no level given) keeps notifications_reason_id nil. update_last_read then auto-tracks rows with a nil reason once the read time passes the threshold, so the user is re-subscribed.

findings.title: No TopicUser row gives NoMethodError (500) for a logged-in user who opens the link
findings.body: `tu` is nil when the user has no topic_users row for a topic they can see; `TopicView.new` at line 99 checks only visibility. Line 107 then calls `.notification_level` on nil. The mailer creates the row only for the recipient (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:312), so a forwarded or shared unsubscribe link opened by another logged-in user returns a 500. Create the row when it is missing (as TopicUser.change does) or return an explicit error.
findings.originReason: The new action dereferences the lookup without a nil check.

verification.reason: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no row, and nothing in the action creates one; TopicView.new only checks visibility. Line 107 then calls `notification_level` on nil, which raises NoMethodError (a 500).

findings.title: The text says notifications stop, but watching and tracking topics are moved to 'regular'
findings.body: For watching or tracking topics the action sets regular (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-108). Regular ranks above muted in the enum (app/models/topic_user.rb:20: muted 0, regular 1, tracking 2, watching 3), so the user may still receive notifications, yet this string says they will stop. Is regular the intended result for those topics? If yes, this text is wrong for them; if no, the controller logic is wrong.
findings.originReason: Both the string and the controller logic are added in this diff.

verification.reason: For watching or tracking topics the controller sets regular (1), not muted (0), so the user can still get notifications, e.g. for replies and mentions. The string says they will stop receiving notifications, so the text and the behaviour disagree.

findings.title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` here and in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3. Rename both to `stopNotificationsText`.

verification.reason: The property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` in both the controller and the template. It works because the two spellings match, but it is a typo.

findings.title: No assertion that the per-topic unsubscribe link is rendered
findings.body: The change only adds `unsubscribe_url` so the constructor call works. The `with add_unsubscribe_link true` block (lines 167-182) checks the List-Unsubscribe header and the preferences URL, not the topic link in `body` or `html_part`. The pull request also adds no spec for `topics#unsubscribe`, so the toggle, the missing-row case and the reason stamp above are untested. Add an expectation that the body includes `unsubscribe_url`, and a request spec for the action.

verification.reason: The spec only passes `unsubscribe_url` and never checks that it appears in the body. No spec under spec/ covers topics#unsubscribe.

contracts.action: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe: toggles the topic notification level and renders the topic page
contracts.before_after: set_notifications goes through TopicUser.change, which stamps notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id=user_changed and publishes notification_level_change (topic_user.rb:87-89, 112-114). unsubscribe does find_by and save! with none of that (topics_controller.rb:105-113).
contracts.visible_effect: perform_show_response renders the topic page with preloaded state after the save (topics_controller.rb:115, 493-501).
contracts.failure_mode: A nil TopicUser raises NoMethodError (topics_controller.rb:105-107). Each fresh GET toggles the level again (topics_controller.rb:107-111). Back or reload re-runs the write.

contracts.action: Ember route topicUnsubscribe model hook loads the topic for the page
contracts.before_after: loadTopicView reads the preloaded topic_<id> payload first and falls back to GET /t/:id.json (post-stream.js.es6:821-823). The fallback hits topics#show, not unsubscribe, so it does not toggle again.
contracts.visible_effect: The template reads topic.details.notification_level through topic-notifications-button (templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:6).
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected load has no catch in the route (routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6-9) and goes to Ember's error state.
contracts.open_question: Does Ember render templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs for the flat route topicUnsubscribe? The dasherized name would be topic-unsubscribe.

contracts.action: Unsubscribe link added to notification emails (html and plain text)
contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/topic.rb:709-711 (Topic#url, the existing absolute topic URL)
contracts.before_after: Before, the footer held only the user-preferences link. Now unsubscribe_url = url + '/unsubscribe' (topic.rb:719-721), and it is absolute because url uses Discourse.base_url (topic.rb:703-707).
contracts.visible_effect: The footer gets a second line in html and in the text body via unsubscribe_link (config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855, app/views/email/notification.html.erb:20, lib/email/message_builder.rb:67-68 and 88-91).
contracts.failure_mode: No failure reachable from this repository: the only caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link is user_notifications.rb:294, and rejection_mailer.rb:9 disallows that key.

contracts.before_after: Before, the h4 was always written, so an unset title rendered the text 'undefined'. Now the h4 is written only when title is truthy.
contracts.visible_effect: Callers without a title (notifications-button, pinned-button) lose the heading element.

contracts.action: perform_show_response renders the topic page through an explicit render :show
contracts.before_after: Before, the implicit render used the current action's template. Now the template is named explicitly, so the unsubscribe action, which has no template of its own, renders topics/show. Callers are show (line 85) and unsubscribe (line 115).
contracts.visible_effect: The topic page HTML for both actions.

contracts.action: Ember route didTransition sets application showFooter to true for the unsubscribe page
contracts.before_after: The same flag and action as the other static pages. Nothing in this part resets it on exit.
contracts.visible_effect: The site footer shows on the unsubscribe page.
contracts.failure_mode: If no later route resets showFooter, it could stay true on other pages. The reset path was not read.
contracts.open_question: Which code resets showFooter when the user leaves the unsubscribe page?

summary: Reviewed the 18 files in this part, reading each in full except `config/routes.rb` (read at 425-454), `config/locales/*.yml` (read at the changed hunks) and `app/models/topic.rb` (read at the changed hunks), plus the Ember and mailer files the new code calls into. The main problems are in the unsubscribe endpoint: (1) it toggles the notification level on a GET request, so a reload or Back moves the level again; (2) because that GET writes state and Rails' CSRF check does not cover GET, a third-party page can trigger the change for a logged-in user; (3) it uses `save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`, which leaves the reason empty, so reading the topic can switch the user back to tracking; (4) a missing TopicUser row gives a 500. Two items need confirmation: whether the template name `topic/unsubscribe.hbs` resolves for the flat route, and whether 'regular' is the intended result for watching and tracking topics. I did not build or run anything.
